newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-KLUIVERT SIGNS FOR AC MILAN IN FOUR-YEAR DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLUIVERT SIGNS FOR AC MILAN IN FOUR-YEAR DEAL.

text.p: Italian giants AC Milan said on Thursday they had signed Dutch striker Patrick Kluivert from Ajax on a four-year contract.

A club statement said Kluivert, one of soccer's brightest talents, would move from Ajax along with utility player Winston Bogarde when their contracts with the Amsterdam club expire at the end of June.
The statement said both players had signed contracts until June 30, 2001. It gave no other details.
Kluivert said last month he wanted to make a fresh start outside the Netherlands. He will join his former Ajax team mates and close friends Edgar Davids and Michael Reiziger at AC Milan.
Ajax, the former European champions, will not receive a transfer fee for the free-scoring 20-year-old.

Apart from AC Milan, city rivals Internazionale, Barcelona, Arsenal and Everton were all reported to be queuing up to pay a rumoured 30 million guilders ($16 million) in wages for his services over four years.
Kluivert said before training on Thursday he was signing a contract with the Italian side.
In the Netherlands, Kluivert has had to face a barrage of terrace taunts after being sentenced to 240 hours community service for causing death by dangerous driving.
AC Milan, too, are desperate for a change of fortune after a dismal season that has seen them suffer surprise exits from the European Cup and the Italian Cup and a run of poor league results.
